card.summary: The Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct Act, or the SCAM Act, makes it illegal for online platforms to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they accept payment for them and fail to take reasonable steps to prevent them. It sets up strict advertiser verification rules, requires platforms to investigate reported scam ads within 72 hours, and removes liability protections under Section 230 for violations. The Federal Trade Commission, state attorneys general, and injured individuals are given enforcement powers.
card.title: SCAM Act

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct Act (or SCAM Act) makes it illegal for online platforms to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they fail to take reasonable prevention steps. The bill requires online platforms to verify advertiser identities, maintain active impersonation detection programs, run fraud detection systems, and provide reporting tools for users. It also sets strict timelines for investigating and removing reported scam ads, establishes Federal Trade Commission and state attorney general enforcement powers, creates a private right of action for injured individuals, and carves out exemptions to Section 230 liability for violations of this act.

affected_groups.effect: Must implement advertiser verification, detection programs, and investigation protocols, and face potential legal liability and penalties for displaying fraudulent paid ads.
Must provide legal names, physical locations, government-issued IDs or business entity documents, and contact information prior to placing paid ads.
Gain tools to report scam advertisements and the ability to bring civil lawsuits for injuries, including triple damages for willful violations and recovery of attorney's fees.
Gain enforcement powers to investigate violations, bring civil actions, obtain damages or restitution, and issue implementing regulations.
affected_groups.group: State Attorneys General and Federal Trade Commission

key_provisions: Makes it unlawful for an online platform to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial ads if it accepted payment and failed to take reasonable prevention steps.
Mandates advertiser identity verification, active impersonation detection programs, automated and manual fraud detection systems, and clear user reporting tools.
Requires online platforms to investigate reported scam ads within 72 hours and remove violating ads within 24 hours of completing an investigation.
Provides a presumption of compliance for platforms that submit a fraud detection program approved and actively enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.
Allows the Federal Trade Commission, state attorneys general, and injured private individuals to bring civil enforcement actions and lawsuits.
Excludes violations of this act from the liability protections found in Section 230(c)(1) of the Communications Act of 1934.
Directs the Federal Trade Commission to submit a report within 9 months assessing whether additional statutory authority is needed to prevent online financial scams.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for civil penalties or fines imposed by the Federal Trade Commission outside of damages awarded in civil lawsuits.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct Act (or SCAM Act) makes it illegal for online platforms to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they fail to take reasonable prevention steps. The bill requires online platforms to verify advertiser identities, maintain active impersonation detection programs, run fraud detection systems, and provide reporting tools for users. It also sets strict timelines for investigating and removing reported scam ads, establishes Federal Trade Commission and state attorney general enforcement powers, creates a private right of action for injured individuals, and carves out exemptions to Section 230 liability for violations of this act.
summary_detail.significance: This bill represents a substantial change in accountability for digital advertising by removing certain Section 230 legal protections for online platforms that display paid fraudulent ads. It imposes direct regulatory mandates, reporting timelines, and private legal liabilities on major technology and social media services.
